document_summary: Part 1 of 3 of Newark, NJ Code Chapter 19:2 (Rent Control Regulations; Rent Control Board), covering the policy statement, definitions, rent increase limits, surcharges, hardship increases and registration provisions. | Part 2 of 3 of Newark, NJ Revised General Ordinances ch. 19:2 (Rent Control), covering registration, rent decreases, hearings, utilities surcharges, new-construction and rehabilitation exemptions, the 25% ceiling on increases and the 2026 inspection provisions. | Part 3 of an ecode360 capture of Newark, NJ Code ch. 19:2 (rent regulation), covering inspection, certificate of habitability, occupancy and registration provisions; it contains no rent cap, just-cause, deposit, screening or algorithmic rent-setting rules.

rules.title: Newark Rent Control: annual CPI-based rent increase cap
rules.requirement: At lease expiration (or termination of a periodic tenancy), a landlord may not request or receive an increase greater than the CPI-U percentage change (15 months prior to 3 months prior to the month of the increase), and never more than 4%. Written notice to the tenant and the Rent Regulation Officer at least 30 days in advance is required. No increase is allowed if the unit is not in substantial compliance or the landlord has not met registration requirements.
rules.key_value: CPI-U increase (NY-Northern NJ-Long Island), max 4% in any consecutive 12-month period
rules.coverage_conditions: All multiple dwellings as defined in § 19:2-2 are subject to rent control (§ 19:2-2.1). The cap applies per housing space in any consecutive twelve-month period, irrespective of tenant turnover, change of ownership or vacancy.
rules.exemptions: Exempt dwellings per § 19:2-2: public housing; hotel/motel space rented day-to-day to transients; commercial space; newly constructed multiple dwellings and vacant dwellings (§§ 19:2-18.1 and 19:2-18.2, not in this part); certain federal/state rehabilitated Section 8 units (rent capped at HUD fair market rent); units under a contract with a governmental agency that regulates rent.
rules.interaction: Board-approved surcharges (tax, major new improvement, hardship, utilities) are separate from this annual cap; the 25% ceiling in § 19:2-22 is not in this part. Local ordinance within NJ framework; no state-level conflict noted in this document.
rules.quoted_span: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of the lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord may request or receive an increase greater than the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) from the CPI 15 months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase to the CPI three months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase. In no case shall the allowable rent increase exceed 4%.
rules.extraction_notes: Section history: Ord. 6 PSF-A(S), 9-5-2017; amended 9-18-2024 by Ord. No. 6PSF-I. Month of adoption; exact effective date not stated in source (NJ ordinances generally take effect after final passage and publication). Latest amendment date used; the document does not show whether the 2024 amendment changed the 4% cap or kept it as originally enacted in 2017. A 2026-06-17 ordinance (6PSF-C) amends only §§ 19:2-27 and 19:2-32 (habitability certificates), not this section. Document is part 1 of 3; § 19:2-18 and § 19:2-22 appear elsewhere.

rules.title: Newark Rent Control: 25% ceiling on Board-granted increases
rules.requirement: The Rent Control Board may not grant increases above 25% in any one year for any tenant. Increases under §§ 19:2-3, 19:2-7 and 19:2-8 within the 12 months before the effective date are added together when testing the 25% limit.
rules.key_value: Board-granted increases capped at 25% of prior monthly rent in any one year
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rent increases granted by the Rent Control Board under Newark's rent control chapter (§§ 19:2-3, 19:2-7, 19:2-8).
rules.interaction: Ceiling on surcharges and increases the Board may grant; the headline annual increase cap is in § 19:2-3, which is not in this part of the document.
rules.quoted_span: Since an immediate rent increase of more than 25% above the prior monthly rent may be considered unconscionable and imposes a hardship on a tenant, the Rent Control Board shall not grant increases exceeding 25% in any one year for any tenant.
rules.extraction_notes: Month of adoption; exact effective date not stated in source (NJ ordinances generally take effect after final passage and publication). History: Ord. 6 PSF-A(S), 9-5-2017; amended 9-18-2024 by Ord. No. 6PSF-I. The chapter's rent control dates from 1985 (see § 19:2-21). Headline cap is in § 19:2-3, outside this part.

rules.title: Newark Rent Control: new construction exemption
rules.requirement: Rent control limits on periodic or regular increases do not apply to newly constructed multiple dwellings for a limited period. The period is the amortization period of the initial mortgage or 30 years after completion of construction, whichever is less.
rules.key_value: New construction exempt from increase limits for the shorter of the initial mortgage amortization period or 30 years
rules.coverage_conditions: Newly constructed multiple dwellings. The landlord must apply to the Rent Control Board for exemption certification after receiving a Certificate of Occupancy or Temporary Certificate of Occupancy and before tenant occupancy. With no initial mortgage financing, the exemption is 30 years from completion of construction.
rules.interaction: Exemption from the headline rent cap, which is in § 19:2-3 (not in this part). The exemption runs with the property, so a change of ownership does not alter it.
rules.quoted_span: The provisions of the Rent Control Ordinance, which limit the periodic or regular increases in base rentals of dwelling units shall not apply to newly constructed multiple dwellings for a period of time not to exceed the period of amortization of any initial mortgage loan obtained for the multiple dwelling, or for 30 years following completion of construction, whichever is less.
rules.extraction_notes: Month of adoption; exact effective date not stated in source (NJ ordinances generally take effect after final passage and publication). Related exemptions in § 19:2-18.2 (vacant 18+ months and rehabilitation cost over 50% of fair market value: 5-year exemption) and § 19:2-18.3 (substantial rehabilitation). Both were amended 5-20-2026 by Ord. 6PSF-B.

rules.title: Newark Rent Control: rehabilitated vacant unit increase (max 10%)
rules.requirement: A landlord who rehabilitates a vacant apartment by spending at least 12 months of actual monthly rent per unit may be granted a one-off increase of up to 10% in the actual monthly rent. Only one such increase is allowed per unit in any twelve-month period.
rules.key_value: Maximum 10% increase after rehabilitating a vacant unit (spend at least 12 months' actual rent)
rules.coverage_conditions: Vacant apartment units rehabilitated at a cost of at least 12 months of actual monthly rent per unit. Requires an affidavit of expenses, an inspection, and abatement of code violations before the increase is granted.
rules.interaction: Special vacancy/rehabilitation increase within Newark rent control; supplements the headline annual cap in § 19:2-3 (not in this part).
rules.quoted_span: Any landlord that rehabilitates a vacant apartment unit by spending a total amount equal to at least 12 months of actual monthly rent per unit will be entitled to a maximum of 10% increase in the actual monthly rent.
rules.extraction_notes: Month of adoption; exact effective date not stated in source (NJ ordinances generally take effect after final passage and publication). History: Ord. 6 PSF-A(S), 9-5-2017; amended 9-18-2024 by Ord. No. 6PSF-I.

rules.title: Newark Rent Control: utilities surcharge ceilings
rules.requirement: A landlord who shows heating and water expenses rose by more than 10% over the prior 12 months is granted a utilities surcharge. The surcharge is capped by building size as a share of the monthly rent roll.
rules.key_value: Surcharge cap: 15% of monthly rent roll (30 or fewer units); 5% (31 to 200 units); 3% (more than 200 units)
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlord must substantiate through credible proof that heating and water expenses (excluding sewer) for the preceding 12 months exceed 10% of the prior 12 months' expenses. The percentage applies to the monthly rent roll in the month the application is submitted.
rules.interaction: Surcharge ceiling within Newark rent control; supplements the headline annual cap in § 19:2-3 (not in this part). Subject to the overall 25% ceiling in § 19:2-22 on Board-granted increases.
rules.quoted_span: However, the increase allowed shall not exceed 15% of the monthly rent roll of apartments which contain 30 or fewer units; and the increase allowed shall not exceed 5% of the monthly rent roll of apartments which contain more than 30 units but less than 201 units; and, the increase allowed shall not exceed 3% of the monthly rent roll of apartments which contain more than 200 units.
rules.extraction_notes: Month of adoption; exact effective date not stated in source (NJ ordinances generally take effect after final passage and publication). Tenants must get one month's written notice of an approved surcharge (§ 19:2-17.7).

rules.title: Newark Rent Control: retaliatory eviction bar
rules.requirement: A landlord may not bring an action to recover possession of a dwelling unit as a reprisal for the tenant's efforts to secure or enforce rights under the rent control chapter.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants asserting rights under Newark's rent control chapter.
rules.quoted_span: No landlord shall bring any action to recover possession of a dwelling unit as a reprisal for the tenant's efforts to secure or enforce any right under this chapter.
rules.out_of_scope_reason: Anti-retaliation provision, not a limit on grounds for eviction; excluded from scope.
rules.extraction_notes: Month of adoption; exact effective date not stated in source (NJ ordinances generally take effect after final passage and publication).
